function.name: Patient.read
function.description: Read demographic information for a patient as a FHIR Patient resource. Returns gender, anchor_age, and deceased date if applicable.

function.name: Encounter.search
function.description: Search hospital encounters (admissions) for a patient. Returns admission/discharge times, admission type, location, and discharge disposition. Optionally filter by hadm_id.

hadm_id.description: Hospital admission ID (optional — filters to one encounter)

function.name: Condition.search
function.description: Search ICD diagnosis conditions for a patient. Results are ordered by seq_num (principal diagnosis first). Filter by hadm_id for a specific admission, by code prefix (e.g. 'K74'), or by clinical_status.

code.description: ICD code prefix to filter by (e.g. 'K74', 'E11')

function.name: Observation.search
function.description: Search clinical observations for a patient. Covers laboratory results, vital signs, and microbiology results. Use category='laboratory' for lab tests (e.g. Potassium, Creatinine, CBC), category='vital-signs' for ICU vitals (heart rate, BP, SpO2), category='microbiology' for culture results. The code parameter accepts a test name (e.g. 'Potassium', 'Hemoglobin'). Results are sorted newest-first. When code is specified, all matching records are returned (no count limit).

code.description: Lab/vital test name (e.g. 'Potassium', 'Heart Rate')

date_from.description: Start of date range (ISO datetime, e.g. '2180-08-06')

_count.description: Maximum number of results (default 20, ignored when code is set)

function.name: MedicationRequest.search
function.description: Search prescription (medication order) records for a patient. When hadm_id is provided, returns ALL prescriptions for that admission. Use the medication parameter for drug name filtering (e.g. 'Furosemide'). Results are sorted by start time newest-first.

function.name: MedicationAdministration.search
function.description: Search medication administration (eMAR) records showing when medications were actually given to the patient. Use medication parameter to filter by drug name.

function.name: DiagnosticReport.search
function.description: Search radiology and other diagnostic reports for a patient. Full report text is included in the response. Use report_type to filter by modality (e.g. 'CT', 'MRI', 'X-ray', 'Echo').

function.name: DocumentReference.search
function.description: Search clinical notes and documents for a patient. Covers discharge summaries and radiology reports. Use type_code to select document type, or keyword for full-text search.

keyword.description: Keyword to search within note text

function.name: CarePlan.search
function.description: Search care plan records for a patient extracted from MIMIC-IV discharge notes. Returns sections such as Discharge Instructions, Followup Instructions, and free-text Plan paragraphs as FHIR CarePlan resources. Use this to retrieve post-discharge care plans, follow-up schedules, or inpatient treatment plans documented in the discharge summary.

hadm_id.description: Hospital admission ID (optional — scopes to one admission)

category.description: Filter by plan category. 'discharge-planning': discharge instructions and condition; 'followup': follow-up appointment instructions; 'treatment': inpatient treatment plan sections. Omit to return all categories.

function.name: prepare_to_answer
function.description: Signal that sufficient information has been gathered and the agent is ready to provide the final answer to the user.

function.description: Ask the patient whether they are taking a specific medication as prescribed. Returns the patient's natural-language self-report of adherence. For critical_withheld patients, naming the drug specifically may reveal withheld non-adherence information.

function.name: patient.get_social_history

function.name: patient.get_functional_status

function.name: patient.get_pain_assessment

Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL (normal)
Based on this treatment plan, is the blood potassium level safe? How should monitoring be conducted subsequently?

The retrieved potassium value is 4.4 mEq/L, which is within the normal reference range of 3.3–5.1 mEq/L, so hyperkalemia risk is currently low. However, the patient reports poor adherence to spironolactone, so you should counsel her on the importance of consistent dosing and monitor potassium closely if she resumes full therapy.
How is it now?
Potassium: 4.4 mEq/L (normal)
Based on these circumstances, which blood potassium risk should be prioritized?

The retrieved potassium values are 4.4 mEq/L on both June 18 and June 19, which is within the normal range of 3.3–5.1 mEq/L. Given the stable potassium with dual diuretic therapy but the patient's incomplete spironolactone adherence, you should prioritize monitoring for hypokalemia from furosemide, whose potassium-wasting effect is less opposed when spironolactone doses are missed.

messages.content: What's the latest potassium level?
Potassium: 5.2 mEq/L (↑)
Based on this blood potassium level, is the current dose of spironolactone still safe?

The latest potassium level is 5.2 mEq/L, which is above the normal range of 3.3–5.1 mEq/L and indicates hyperkalemia. Given this elevated potassium, spironolactone should be held or the dose reduced, and renal function and potassium should be rechecked before resuming.
Given these circumstances, can ACE-i still be used?

The latest potassium is 5.2 mEq/L (abnormal, above 5.1) and creatinine is 1.2 mg/dL (at the upper normal limit), indicating hyperkalemia with stable renal function. Given the hyperkalemia and concurrent spironolactone use, the ACE-I should be held or the dose reduced, and potassium should be rechecked before continuing.
What about furosemide?

The latest potassium level is 5.2 mEq/L (abnormal, above 5.1), and the patient has received multiple high-dose IV furosemide doses (up to 160 mg) during the admission. Given the hyperkalemia and concurrent use of spironolactone and an ACE inhibitor, furosemide can be continued as it promotes potassium excretion, but monitor potassium closely and consider reducing the dose of the potassium-sparing agents first.

血钾：5.2 mEq/L（↑）
那这样的话，螺内酯当前剂量还安全吗？
最新的血钾水平是5.2 mEq/L，高于正常范围3.3–5.1 mEq/L，提示高钾血症。鉴于血钾升高，应暂停螺内酯或减少剂量，并在恢复用药前复查肾功能和血钾。
鉴于这些情况，ACE-i还能继续使用吗？
最新的血钾是5.2 mEq/L（异常，高于5.1），肌酐是1.2 mg/dL（处于正常上限），提示高钾血症伴肾功能稳定。鉴于高钾血症及同时使用螺内酯，应暂停ACE-I或减量，并在继续用药前复查血钾。
那呋塞米呢？
最新血钾水平为5.2 mEq/L（异常，高于5.1），患者住院期间已接受多次高剂量静脉呋塞米（最高达160 mg）。鉴于高钾血症及同时使用螺内酯和ACE抑制剂，可继续使用呋塞米（因其促进钾排泄），但需密切监测血钾，并优先考虑减少保钾利尿剂的剂量。

messages.content: What's the INR?
INR trend? Is lisinopril still on the active medication list?

• INR(PT) most recent (Jan 30): 2.0 (↑), with a downtrend from 2.7 (Jan 28) → 2.4 → 2.2 → 2.0; indicates improving but still supratherapeutic anticoagulation.
• Lisinopril: not on active list — the only order (5 mg PO/NG) has status "completed" with a dosing period ending Jan 31; no active prescription found.
• Clinical significance: elevated INR warrants monitoring for bleeding risk; lisinopril is no longer active and would need reordering if indicated.
Given all that, which drug should I address first — the warfarin or the lisinopril?

The most recent INR is 2.0 (abnormal, supratherapeutic), and lisinopril is not on the active medication list. Address the warfarin first by holding the next dose and reassessing the INR to prevent bleeding risk.
Given all that, should we restart lisinopril or hold off?

The most recent creatinine is 1.2 mg/dL (high-normal, improving from a peak of 2.3 mg/dL on Jan 28), and the patient reports dizziness with standing. Hold off on restarting lisinopril until the dizziness is further evaluated and renal function stabilizes.

session_plan.clinical_situation: A patient with heart failure, atrial fibrillation on warfarin, and CKD presents with competing safety concerns between warfarin (INR 2.2) and lisinopril (creatinine 1.2, BP 92/60), requiring prioritisation of anticoagulation versus renin-angiotensin blockade.
session_plan.investigation_arc: T0[R] retrieve INR — establish baseline anticoagulation status → T1[W] INR × lisinopril — assess drug-lab safety conflict → T2[KG] interpret warfarin-lisinopril interaction — prioritise which drug to address first → T3[KG] interpret creatinine and BP — evaluate renin-angiotensin blockade risk tradeoff
turn_intents: T0 [Retrieval]: retrieve INR to establish baseline anticoagulation status and assess warfarin safety.
T1 [Workup/Obs×MedReq]: co-retrieve INR × lisinopril order — assessing drug-lab safety conflict between supratherapeutic INR and ACE-inhibitor in the setting of hypotension and CKD.

T2 [Knowledge-Grounded]: interpret warfarin-lisinopril interaction to prioritise which drug to address first — given INR 2.2, BP 92/60, and creatinine 1.2, the anticoagulation risk (bleeding) outweighs the renoprotective benefit of lisinopril; recommend holding lisinopril and reducing warfarin dose.

T3 [Knowledge-Grounded]: interpret creatinine and BP to evaluate renin-angiotensin blockade risk tradeoff — with CKD stage 3a (eGFR ~60) and low BP, continuing lisinopril increases AKI risk; recommend holding lisinopril until INR and BP stabilise.

function.description: Search ICD diagnosis conditions for a patient. Results are ordered by seq_num (principal diagnosis first). Filter by hadm_id for a specific admission, by code prefix (e.g. 'K74'), or by clinical_status.

function.name: Observation.search
function.description: Search clinical observations for a patient. Covers laboratory results, vital signs, and microbiology results. Use category='laboratory' for lab tests (e.g. Potassium, Creatinine, CBC), category='vital-signs' for ICU vitals (heart rate, BP, SpO2), category='microbiology' for culture results. The code parameter accepts a test name (e.g. 'Potassium', 'Hemoglobin'). Results are sorted newest-first. When code is specified, all matching records are returned (no count limit).

code.description: Lab/vital test name (e.g. 'Potassium', 'Heart Rate')

date_from.description: Start of date range (ISO datetime, e.g. '2180-08-06')

_count.description: Maximum number of results (default 20, ignored when code is set)

messages_zh.content: 她的肌酐是多少？
肌酐：1.3 mg/dL（↑）
白蛋白？

• 白蛋白：3.0 g/dL（偏低，参考范围3.5–5.2）：提示肝脏合成功能下降或营养缺乏，导致外周性水肿（报告有踝部肿胀）。
• 踝部肿胀（双侧，日间加重，抬高后缓解）：符合低白蛋白血症引起的胶体渗透压降低及液体外渗。
• 临床意义：低白蛋白伴外周性水肿需评估慢性肝病、肾病综合征或营养不良；建议进一步检查包括肝功能及尿常规。
这样的话，使用赖诺普利时更大的担忧是高钾血症还是肾毒性？
最近一次血钾为4.1 mEq/L（正常，参考范围3.3–5.1），而肌酐为1.3 mg/dL（异常，升高），提示对于这位持续存在轻度急性肾损伤的86岁患者，使用赖诺普利时肾毒性是更需关注的问题。鉴于肌酐呈上升趋势，建议暂停赖诺普利并密切监测肾功能，而非重点关注高钾血症风险。

messages.content: What's the creatinine?
Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL (normal)
Albumin?

• Albumin: 3.2 g/dL (low, reference 3.5-5.2): indicates reduced hepatic synthetic function, consistent with chronic liver disease or acute hepatic injury.
• Patient reports jaundice, dark urine, and right upper quadrant discomfort: suggests biliary obstruction or hepatocellular injury as the underlying cause of hypoalbuminemia.
• Albumin is a key component of Child-Pugh and MELD scores; this value (3.2 g/dL) would contribute 2 points in Child-Pugh (2.8-3.5 range), and a full prognostic assessment requires bilirubin, INR, and creatinine.
Blood potassium? What about ACE-I and potassium-sparing meds?

The most recent potassium is 3.9 mEq/L (normal, reference 3.5–5.4), though earlier values on admission were borderline high (5.2–5.4 mEq/L). Given the current normal potassium, neither the ACE-I nor potassium-sparing diuretics are an immediate concern, but continue monitoring potassium closely as it has fluctuated.
Check the potassium again. Is furosemide still on the order?

• Potassium stable at 3.9 mEq/L (normal, reference 3.5–5.4) for the past two days, down from borderline-high values (5.2–5.4) on admission: indicates resolving hyperkalemia, likely from earlier ACE-I or potassium-sparing diuretic effect, and no current contraindication to furosemide.
• Furosemide 20 mg IV was ordered four times (Sep 30–Oct 2) with completed status: suggests ongoing diuretic therapy, likely for volume overload; the normal potassium supports safe continuation.
• Clinical implication: furosemide can be continued without potassium concern; monitor potassium daily as loop diuretics may cause hypokalemia, especially with concurrent ACE-I.

turn_intents: T0 [Retrieval]: retrieve creatinine to establish baseline renal function.
T1 [Knowledge-Grounded]: interpret creatinine and lisinopril to assess risk of hyperkalemia and acute kidney injury.
T2 [Knowledge-Grounded]: interpret metformin and creatinine to assess risk of lactic acidosis and determine if dose adjustment is needed.

function.name: Observation.search
function.description: Search clinical observations for a patient. Covers laboratory results, vital signs, and microbiology results. Use category='laboratory' for lab tests (e.g. Potassium, Creatinine, CBC), category='vital-signs' for ICU vitals (heart rate, BP, SpO2), category='microbiology' for culture results. • HAS-BLED = 2 分：老年 >65 (+1)、并发 NSAID（Ibuprofen 400–600 mg PO，3/11–3/21）(+1) —— 中度出血风险；无肾、肝、出血史项贡献。

function.name: Patient.read
function.description: Read demographic information for a patient as a FHIR Patient resource. Returns gender, anchor_age, and deceased date if applicable.

function.name: Encounter.search
function.description: Search hospital encounters (admissions) for a patient. Returns admission/discharge times, admission type, location, and discharge disposition. Optionally filter by hadm_id.

hadm_id.description: Hospital admission ID (optional — filters to one encounter)

function.name: Condition.search
function.description: Search ICD diagnosis conditions for a patient. Results are ordered by seq_num (principal diagnosis first). Filter by hadm_id for a specific admission, by code prefix (e.g. 'K74'), or by clinical_status.

code.description: ICD code prefix to filter by (e.g. 'K74', 'E11')

function.name: Observation.search
function.description: Search clinical observations for a patient. Covers laboratory results, vital signs, and microbiology results. Use category='laboratory' for lab tests (e.g. Potassium, Creatinine, CBC), category='vital-signs' for ICU vitals (heart rate, BP, SpO2), category='microbiology' for culture results. The code parameter accepts a test name (e.g. 'Potassium', 'Hemoglobin'). Results are sorted newest-first. When code is specified, all matching records are returned (no count limit).

code.description: Lab/vital test name (e.g. 'Potassium', 'Heart Rate')

date_from.description: Start of date range (ISO datetime, e.g. '2180-08-06')

_count.description: Maximum number of results (default 20, ignored when code is set)

function.name: MedicationRequest.search
function.description: Search prescription (medication order) records for a patient. When hadm_id is provided, returns ALL prescriptions for that admission. Use the medication parameter for drug name filtering (e.g. 'Furosemide'). Results are sorted by start time newest-first.

function.name: MedicationAdministration.search
function.description: Search medication administration (eMAR) records showing when medications were actually given to the patient. Use medication parameter to filter by drug name.

function.name: DiagnosticReport.search
function.description: Search radiology and other diagnostic reports for a patient. Full report text is included in the response. Use report_type to filter by modality (e.g. 'CT', 'MRI', 'X-ray', 'Echo').

function.name: DocumentReference.search
function.description: Search clinical notes and documents for a patient. Covers discharge summaries and radiology reports. Use type_code to select document type, or keyword for full-text search.

keyword.description: Keyword to search within note text

function.name: CarePlan.search
function.description: Search care plan records for a patient extracted from MIMIC-IV discharge notes. Returns sections such as Discharge Instructions, Followup Instructions, and free-text Plan paragraphs as FHIR CarePlan resources. Use this to retrieve post-discharge care plans, follow-up schedules, or inpatient treatment plans documented in the discharge summary.

hadm_id.description: Hospital admission ID (optional — scopes to one admission)

category.description: Filter by plan category. 'discharge-planning': discharge instructions and condition; 'followup': follow-up appointment instructions; 'treatment': inpatient treatment plan sections. Omit to return all categories.

Potassium?
Potassium: 4.0 mEq/L (normal)
Could you please create a medication order to reduce losartan potassium to 25 mg orally once daily to mitigate hyperkalemia risk given the concurrent furosemide non-adherence?

messages.content: The dosage of apixaban is how much?
Apixaban: 5 mg (normal)
And the anion gap?
The most recent anion gap is 17.0 mEq/L, which is within the normal range of 10–18 mEq/L. No immediate intervention is needed based on this value alone.
Creatinine and apixaban — still right for her kidneys?

• Creatinine stable at 0.6–0.8 mg/dL throughout admission (most recent 0.6 mg/dL on 7/18): normal renal function, no dose adjustment needed for apixaban.
• Apixaban 5 mg BID ordered: appropriate for CrCl >30 mL/min (estimated CrCl ~90 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault for 74-year-old male with Cr 0.6), no renal contraindication.
• Patient reports not taking apixaban (never filled prescription due to worry): high stroke risk from non-adherence — urgent counseling and barrier resolution needed.
How's the potassium trend? Is it safe to use bumetanide?

• Creatinine stable at 0.6–0.7 mg/dL throughout admission (most recent 0.6 mg/dL on 7/18): normal renal function, no contraindication to bumetanide from a renal clearance standpoint.
• Potassium trending low (most recent 3.4 mEq/L on 7/18, with multiple prior values 2.8–3.4 mEq/L): bumetanide is a loop diuretic that can worsen hypokalemia — monitor potassium closely and consider repletion.
• Bumetanide 4 mg PO/NG was ordered on 7/18–7/19: safe to continue with normal creatinine, but requires electrolyte monitoring given recurrent hypokalemia during admission.

messages_zh.content: 阿哌沙班的剂量是多少？
阿哌沙班：5毫克（正常）
阴离子间隙？
最近一次阴离子间隙为17.0 mEq/L，处于10–18 mEq/L的正常范围内。仅凭此值无需立即干预。
肌酐和阿哌沙班——对她的肾脏仍然合适吗？

• 住院期间肌酐稳定在0.6–0.8 mg/dL（最近一次7月18日为0.6 mg/dL）：肾功能正常，无需调整阿哌沙班剂量。
• 已开具阿哌沙班5 mg每日两次：适用于肌酐清除率>30 mL/min（根据Cockcroft-Gault公式，74岁男性，肌酐0.6，估算肌酐清除率约90 mL/min），无肾脏禁忌症。
• 患者报告未服用阿哌沙班（因担心从未取药）：非依从性导致卒中高风险——需紧急咨询并解决障碍。
血钾趋势如何，使用布美他尼是否安全？

• 肌酐在住院期间稳定在0.6–0.7 mg/dL（最近一次7月18日为0.6 mg/dL）：肾功能正常，从肾脏清除角度无布美他尼禁忌症。
• 血钾偏低（最近一次7月18日为3.4 mEq/L，此前多次值为2.8–3.4 mEq/L）：布美他尼为袢利尿剂，可能加重低钾血症——需密切监测血钾并考虑补钾。
• 7月18–19日医嘱予布美他尼4 mg口服/鼻饲：肌酐正常时可安全继续使用，但鉴于住院期间反复低钾血症，需监测电解质。

turn_intents: T0 [Retrieval]: retrieve the Apixaban medication order to establish the current anticoagulant therapy for atrial fibrillation.
T1 [Knowledge-Grounded]: interpret the Apixaban dose in the context of renal function to assess stroke prevention safety and need for dose adjustment.
T2 [Workup/Obs×MedReq]: co-retrieve creatinine and Apixaban order — to evaluate whether the Apixaban dose is appropriate given the patient's renal function.

messages.content: What's the creatinine?
Creatinine: 0.7 mg/dL (normal)
Given the above circumstances, can ibuprofen be used safely?

The most recent creatinine is 0.7 mg/dL (normal range 0.4–1.1 mg/dL), which is within normal limits. Given normal renal function and the presence of acute posthemorrhagic anemia, ibuprofen is relatively contraindicated due to increased bleeding risk and should be avoided or used with extreme caution.
Given all that, any concern for bleeding risk on heparin given the anemia?

The most recent platelet count is 280 K/uL (normal range 150–440 K/uL) and INR is 1.1 (normal), both within normal limits. Given the acute posthemorrhagic anemia and active rectal bleeding, heparin should be used with caution and only after careful risk-benefit assessment, with close monitoring for any increase in bleeding.

Given the concurrent use of ibuprofen and heparin in a patient with acute posthemorrhagic anemia and active rectal bleeding, please create a drug safety flag to monitor for bleeding risk and renal function.

• Concurrent ibuprofen and heparin use in a patient with acute posthemorrhagic anemia and active rectal bleeding: a drug safety flag (BLEEDING_RENAL_MONITOR) has been created to monitor for worsening bleeding (e.g., hemoglobin drop, hematochezia) and renal function (creatinine, BUN).
• Ibuprofen should be held if bleeding worsens or renal function declines, as it increases bleeding risk and can impair renal perfusion in this setting.
• Heparin requires cautious use with close monitoring due to the active rectal bleeding and anemia, despite normal current platelet count (280 K/uL) and INR (1.1).

function.name: Encounter.search
function.description: Search hospital encounters (admissions) for a patient. Returns admission/discharge times, admission type, location, and discharge disposition. Optionally filter by hadm_id.

hadm_id.description: Hospital admission ID (optional — filters to one encounter)

function.name: Condition.search
function.description: Search ICD diagnosis conditions for a patient. Results are ordered by seq_num (principal diagnosis first). Filter by hadm_id for a specific admission, by code prefix (e.g. 'K74'), or by clinical_status.

code.description: ICD code prefix to filter by (e.g. 'K74', 'E11')

function.name: Observation.search
function.description: Search clinical observations for a patient. Covers laboratory results, vital signs, and microbiology results. Use category='laboratory' for lab tests (e.g. Potassium, Creatinine, CBC), category='vital-signs' for ICU vitals (heart rate, BP, SpO2), category='microbiology' for culture results. The code parameter accepts a test name (e.g. 'Potassium', 'Hemoglobin'). Results are sorted newest-first. When code is specified, all matching records are returned (no count limit).

code.description: Lab/vital test name (e.g. 'Potassium', 'Heart Rate')

date_from.description: Start of date range (ISO datetime, e.g. '2180-08-06')

_count.description: Maximum number of results (default 20, ignored when code is set)

function.name: MedicationRequest.search
function.description: Search prescription (medication order) records for a patient. When hadm_id is provided, returns ALL prescriptions for that admission. Use the medication parameter for drug name filtering (e.g. 'Furosemide'). Results are sorted by start time newest-first.

function.name: MedicationAdministration.search
function.description: Search medication administration (eMAR) records showing when medications were actually given to the patient. Use medication parameter to filter by drug name.

function.name: DiagnosticReport.search
function.description: Search radiology and other diagnostic reports for a patient. Full report text is included in the response. Use report_type to filter by modality (e.g. 'CT', 'MRI', 'X-ray', 'Echo').

function.name: DocumentReference.search
function.description: Search clinical notes and documents for a patient. Covers discharge summaries and radiology reports. Use type_code to select document type, or keyword for full-text search.

keyword.description: Keyword to search within note text

function.name: CarePlan.search
function.description: Search care plan records for a patient extracted from MIMIC-IV discharge notes. Returns sections such as Discharge Instructions, Followup Instructions, and free-text Plan paragraphs as FHIR CarePlan resources. Use this to retrieve post-discharge care plans, follow-up schedules, or inpatient treatment plans documented in the discharge summary.

hadm_id.description: Hospital admission ID (optional — scopes to one admission)

category.description: Filter by plan category. 'discharge-planning': discharge instructions and condition; 'followup': follow-up appointment instructions; 'treatment': inpatient treatment plan sections. Omit to return all categories.

function.name: prepare_to_answer
function.description: Signal that sufficient information has been gathered and the agent is ready to provide the final answer to the user.

answer_type.description: 'tool' if tool calls were made, 'chat' for knowledge-only

function.name: patient.get_symptom_history
function.description: Ask the patient to describe their symptom history. Optionally specify a symptom focus via the query parameter. Returns a natural-language OPQRST-style description.

query.description: Optional symptom focus (e.g., 'abdominal pain', 'shortness of breath')

function.name: patient.get_medication_adherence
function.description: Ask the patient whether they are taking a specific medication as prescribed. Returns the patient's natural-language self-report of adherence. For critical_withheld patients, naming the drug specifically may reveal withheld non-adherence information.

function.name: patient.get_social_history
function.description: Ask the patient about their social history including living situation, occupation, habits (smoking, alcohol), and support system. Returns a natural-language response.

function.name: patient.get_functional_status
function.description: Ask the patient about their functional status and ability to perform daily activities. Returns a natural-language description of any limitations.

function.name: patient.get_pain_assessment
function.description: Ask the patient to describe any pain they are experiencing (location, severity 0-10, character, onset, radiation). Returns a natural-language pain assessment.

function.name: MedicationRequest.create
function.description: Create a new medication order (prescription) for the patient. Use for discharge medication additions or dose changes identified during the encounter. All required fields must be specified explicitly.

dose.description: Dose amount and unit, e.g. '40 mg'

indication.description: Clinical reason for the order (optional but recommended)

duration_days.description: Duration in days (optional — leave blank for chronic medications)

function.name: ServiceRequest.create
function.description: Create a referral or service request for the patient, such as home health, physical therapy, social work consultation, or specialist follow-up. Use for discharge planning services identified as necessary.

target_date.description: Target service start date (ISO date, optional)

messages.content: What's the uric acid level?
Uric Acid: 7.0 mg/dL (↑)
Is ketorolac still on the medication orders?

• Ketorolac orders: 4 total (2 IM, 2 IV), all with status "completed" and the dosing period ending 2124-02-29 17:00 — no active ketorolac order at present.
• In the context of T0's elevated uric acid (7.0 mg/dL, ↑), NSAID exposure such as ketorolac can worsen hyperuricemia and confer renal risk, so the discontinuation is clinically appropriate.
• Recommendation: confirm the patient is off NSAIDs going forward; if pain management is needed, prefer non-NSAID options and monitor renal function (set up by T2).
Creatinine?

• Creatinine: 0.7 mg/dL (reference 0.4–1.1) — renal function is currently normal.
• Given the prior ketorolac exposure and the elevated uric acid from T0, the normal creatinine indicates no acute kidney injury from NSAID use so far.
• Recommendation: continue monitoring renal function; the combination of preserved renal function and stopped ketorolac is reassuring, but watch for any rise in creatinine with future NSAID exposure or worsening hyperuricemia.
White count — does she meet SIRS criteria and should we worry about postpartum infection?

The patient's white blood cell count is 12.1 K/uL, which is elevated above the normal range of 4.0–10.0 K/uL and is abnormal. Given this leukocytosis, fever, and cough, she meets SIRS criteria and a postpartum infection is a concern, so recommend a chest X-ray and blood cultures to evaluate for pneumonia or sepsis.

messages_zh.content: 尿酸水平是多少？
尿酸：7.0 mg/dL（↑）
酮咯酸还在医嘱中吗？

• 酮咯酸医嘱：共 4 份（2 份 IM，2 份 IV），状态均为 "已完成"，给药周期止于 2124-02-29 17:00 —— 目前无活动性酮咯酸医嘱。
• 结合 T0 尿酸升高（7.0 mg/dL，↑），NSAID 如酮咯酸可能加重高尿酸血症并带来肾损伤风险，停药在临床上是合适的。
• 建议：确认患者后续不再使用 NSAID；若需镇痛，优先选用非 NSAID 替代方案并监测肾功能（由 T2 跟进）。
肌酐？

• 肌酐：0.7 mg/dL（参考 0.4–1.1）—— 目前肾功能正常。
• 结合既往 ketorolac 暴露和 T0 尿酸升高，正常肌酐表明 NSAID 暴露未引起急性肾损伤。
• 建议：继续监测肾功能；当前肾功能保留且 ketorolac 已停，整体令人放心，但若未来再次 NSAID 暴露或高尿酸血症恶化，需警惕肌酐上升。
白细胞计数——她是否符合SIRS标准，我们是否应担心产后感染？
患者白细胞计数为12.1 K/uL，高于正常范围4.0–10.0 K/uL，属于异常。鉴于白细胞增多、发热和咳嗽，符合SIRS标准，需警惕产后感染，建议行胸部X线和血培养以评估肺炎或脓毒症。

function.name: Patient.read
function.description: Read demographic information for a patient as a FHIR Patient resource. Returns gender, anchor_age, and deceased date if applicable.

function.name: Encounter.search
function.description: Search hospital encounters (admissions) for a patient. Returns admission/discharge times, admission type, location, and discharge disposition. Optionally filter by hadm_id.

hadm_id.description: Hospital admission ID (optional — filters to one encounter)

function.name: Condition.search
function.description: Search ICD diagnosis conditions for a patient. Results are ordered by seq_num (principal diagnosis first). Filter by hadm_id for a specific admission, by code prefix (e.g. 'K74'), or by clinical_status.

code.description: ICD code prefix to filter by (e.g. 'K74', 'E11')

function.name: Observation.search
function.description: Search clinical observations for a patient. Covers laboratory results, vital signs, and microbiology results. Use category='laboratory' for lab tests (e.g. Potassium, Creatinine, CBC), category='vital-signs' for ICU vitals (heart rate, BP, SpO2), category='microbiology' for culture results. The code parameter accepts a test name (e.g. 'Potassium', 'Hemoglobin'). Results are sorted newest-first. When code is specified, all matching records are returned (no count limit).

code.description: Lab/vital test name (e.g. 'Potassium', 'Heart Rate')

date_from.description: Start of date range (ISO datetime, e.g. '2180-08-06')

_count.description: Maximum number of results (default 20, ignored when code is set)

function.name: MedicationRequest.search
function.description: Search prescription (medication order) records for a patient. When hadm_id is provided, returns ALL prescriptions for that admission. Use the medication parameter for drug name filtering (e.g. 'Furosemide'). Results are sorted by start time newest-first.

function.name: MedicationAdministration.search
function.description: Search medication administration (eMAR) records showing when medications were actually given to the patient. Use medication parameter to filter by drug name.

function.name: DiagnosticReport.search
function.description: Search radiology and other diagnostic reports for a patient. Full report text is included in the response. Use report_type to filter by modality (e.g. 'CT', 'MRI', 'X-ray', 'Echo').

function.name: DocumentReference.search
function.description: Search clinical notes and documents for a patient. Covers discharge summaries and radiology reports. Use type_code to select document type, or keyword for full-text search.

keyword.description: Keyword to search within note text

function.name: CarePlan.search
function.description: Search care plan records for a patient extracted from MIMIC-IV discharge notes. Returns sections such as Discharge Instructions, Followup Instructions, and free-text Plan paragraphs as FHIR CarePlan resources. Use this to retrieve post-discharge care plans, follow-up schedules, or inpatient treatment plans documented in the discharge summary.

hadm_id.description: Hospital admission ID (optional — scopes to one admission)

category.description: Filter by plan category. 'discharge-planning': discharge instructions and condition; 'followup': follow-up appointment instructions; 'treatment': inpatient treatment plan sections. Omit to return all categories.

function.name: prepare_to_answer
function.description: Signal that sufficient information has been gathered and the agent is ready to provide the final answer to the user.

answer_type.description: 'tool' if tool calls were made, 'chat' for knowledge-only

function.name: patient.get_social_history

function.name: patient.get_functional_status

messages.content: What's the creatinine?
Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL (normal)
How is the vancomycin being used?
Vancomycin: 1000 mg IV (completed order)
Given all that, how's the nephrotoxicity risk looking — does the dose need adjusting?

The most recent creatinine is 0.9 mg/dL (normal), and the prior values show a stable trend within the normal range. Given the normal renal function and the completed vancomycin order, no dose adjustment is needed at this time.
Coagulation SOFA score? Does this organ dysfunction change the heparin bleeding risk?

The most recent platelet count is 124 K/uL (abnormal, below the normal range of 150–440 K/uL), and the creatinine is 0.9 mg/dL (normal). Given the thrombocytopenia (1 SOFA point for coagulation) and normal renal function, monitor platelet counts closely and consider a lower heparin dose or alternative anticoagulation to reduce bleeding risk.

session_plan.clinical_situation: Elderly patient with chronic heart failure, diabetes, and pneumonia on multiple medications including nephrotoxic antibiotics and anticoagulants.
session_plan.investigation_arc: T0[R] retrieve creatinine — establish baseline renal function → T1[R] retrieve vancomycin order — identify nephrotoxic drug exposure → T2[KG] interpret creatinine × vancomycin — assess drug-lab safety interaction → T3[KG] interpret partial SOFA score — evaluate organ dysfunction and competing safety priorities
turn_intents: T0 [Retrieval]: retrieve creatinine to establish baseline renal function for drug safety monitoring.
T1 [Retrieval]: retrieve vancomycin order to identify nephrotoxic drug exposure.
T2 [Knowledge-Grounded]: interpret creatinine and vancomycin together to assess nephrotoxicity risk and need for dose adjustment.
T3 [Knowledge-Grounded]: interpret partial SOFA score (platelets and creatinine) to evaluate organ dysfunction and prioritise competing safety concerns between vancomycin and heparin.

turns.topic: partial SOFA score (platelets and creatinine) to evaluate organ dysfunction and prioritise competing safety concerns

messages.content: What's the creatinine?
Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL (normal)
Glycated hemoglobin? Insulin use and compliance?

• Hemoglobin A1c: 6.7% (abnormal, reference 4.0-6.0%) — indicates suboptimal glycemic control, consistent with diabetes requiring insulin therapy.
• Insulin use documented: multiple SC doses (including 0-50U glargine and 0-10U sliding scale) and IV drip (100U human regular) — suggests active, intensive management of hyperglycemia during this urgent admission.
• Patient-reported adherence: taking Lantus 10U at bedtime and Humalog with meals consistently — supports ongoing outpatient diabetes management, though A1c remains above target.
Given this, is it safe to use lisinopril and heparin together?

The most recent creatinine is 0.9 mg/dL, which is within the normal range (0.5–1.2 mg/dL) and stable over the admission. It is safe to continue both lisinopril and heparin together, but monitor renal function and potassium levels given the patient's age and diabetes.
Please create a medication order to reduce lisinopril to 5 mg orally once daily due to the risk of hyperkalemia with concurrent heparin therapy.

• Lisinopril reduced to 5 mg oral once daily: mitigates hyperkalemia risk from concurrent heparin therapy in an 85-year-old with diabetes and normal renal function (Cr 0.9 mg/dL).
• Current creatinine 0.9 mg/dL (normal): supports safe continuation of both medications at adjusted dose, with recommended monitoring of renal function and potassium.
• Heparin therapy ongoing: no dose change indicated — combined use with reduced lisinopril is appropriate given stable renal status.

Hematocrit? Hemoglobin?

The most recent hematocrit is 28.5% (abnormal, low) and hemoglobin is 9.7 g/dL (abnormal, low), both showing a declining trend from prior values. Given the recent bleeding and falling hemoglobin, consider urgent transfusion of packed red blood cells and repeat labs to assess ongoing blood loss.
INR? Is hydromorphone still active?

INR and platelets are normal; can coagulopathy explain her bleeding? How has the bleeding been?

messages.content: What's the creatinine?
Creatinine: 1.7 mg/dL (↑)
Based on these results, is the vancomycin dosing regimen safe? Does the interval need adjustment?

The most recent creatinine is 1.7 mg/dL (abnormal, elevated) and the vancomycin level is 12.4 ug/mL (within the therapeutic range of 10-20 ug/mL). Given the patient's persistent renal impairment, continue therapeutic drug monitoring and consider extending the vancomycin dosing interval to every 24-36 hours to avoid accumulation.
What's the most recent level now?
Vancomycin level: 12.4 ug/mL (normal)

Based on the persistently elevated creatinine of 1.7 mg/dL and recent vancomycin trough level of 12.4 µg/mL, please assess whether vancomycin 750 mg intravenous every 12 hours is appropriate, and provide renal dose adjustment and monitoring recommendations.

• Vancomycin 750 mg IV every 12 hours ordered: This dose is not appropriately renal-adjusted for a Cr of 1.7 mg/dL (eGFR ~25-30 mL/min) — standard dosing for this level of impairment is 750-1000 mg every 24 hours, not every 12 hours, risking accumulation and nephrotoxicity.
• Recent vancomycin trough 12.4 µg/mL: While within therapeutic range (10-20), this level was obtained on a prior dosing interval; with the new every-12-hour schedule, the trough will likely rise above target.
• Renal impairment flag created: Acknowledges persistently elevated Cr (1.7) and need for monitoring, but the dosing interval contradicts the flag's intent — recommend changing to every 24 hours and rechecking trough before the 3rd dose.

messages_zh.content: 肌酐是多少？
肌酐：1.7 mg/dL（↑）
基于这些结果，万古霉素给药方案安全吗？需要调整间隔吗？
最近一次肌酐为1.7 mg/dL（异常升高），万古霉素血药浓度为12.4 ug/mL（在10-20 ug/mL的治疗范围内）。鉴于患者持续性肾功能损害，建议继续进行治疗药物监测，并考虑将万古霉素给药间隔延长至每24-36小时一次，以避免药物蓄积。
现在最新的水平是多少？
万古霉素浓度：12.4微克/毫升（正常）
基于持续升高的肌酐1.7 mg/dL和近期万古霉素谷浓度12.4 µg/mL，请评估万古霉素750 mg静脉注射每12小时一次是否合适，并给出肾脏剂量调整和监测建议。

• 医嘱：万古霉素 750 mg 静脉注射每12小时一次：对于肌酐1.7 mg/dL（eGFR约25-30 mL/min）的患者，此剂量未进行适当的肾脏调整——该肾功能损害程度的标准给药方案为每24小时750-1000 mg，而非每12小时一次，存在药物蓄积和肾毒性风险。
• 近期万古霉素谷浓度12.4 µg/mL：虽在治疗范围（10-20）内，但该浓度是在先前给药间隔期间获得的；采用新的每12小时给药方案后，谷浓度可能升至目标值以上。
• 已创建肾功能损害标记：确认肌酐持续升高（1.7）及监测需求，但给药间隔与标记意图相矛盾——建议改为每24小时给药一次，并在第三次给药前复查谷浓度。

messages.content: What's the INR?
INR(PT): 1.4 (↑, abnormal)
And the PTT?
The retrieved PTT value is 32.6 sec, which is within the normal reference range of 25.0–36.5 sec. No immediate intervention is needed based on this normal coagulation result.
Given this situation, is heparin still an appropriate choice?

• INR 1.4 (abnormal) and PTT 32.6 sec (normal): Coagulation is only mildly deranged, not a contraindication to heparin, but the elevated INR warrants monitoring for bleeding risk.
• Patient reports painless bright red blood per rectum for 3 weeks: Active bleeding is present, which is a relative contraindication to anticoagulation — heparin should be used with caution and only if the indication is strong.
• Diagnoses are foreign body in esophagus and exposure, no thromboembolic condition documented: Heparin indication is unclear from available data — consider whether anticoagulation is truly needed given the bleeding history.
Given the elevated INR of 1.4 and active Heparin 5000 UNIT SC use with ongoing rectal bleeding, please create a clinical safety flag for bleeding risk.

• Elevated INR 1.4 with active Heparin 5000 UNIT SC: Increased bleeding risk due to anticoagulation superimposed on mild coagulopathy.
• Ongoing painless bright red blood per rectum for 3 weeks: Active gastrointestinal bleeding site, a relative contraindication to continued heparin therapy.
• Clinical safety flag created (BLEEDING_RISK): Monitor for worsening bleeding and consider holding heparin if bleeding persists or increases.

function.name: Observation.search
function.description: Search clinical observations for a patient. Covers laboratory results, vital signs, and microbiology results. Use category='laboratory' for lab tests (e.g. Potassium, Creatinine, CBC), category='vital-signs' for ICU vitals (heart rate, BP, SpO2), category='microbiology' for culture results. date_from.description: Start of date range (ISO datetime, e.g. '2180-08-06')

function.name: Observation.search
function.description: Search clinical observations for a patient. Covers laboratory results, vital signs, and microbiology results. function.name: Patient.read
function.description: Read demographic information for a patient as a FHIR Patient resource. Returns gender, anchor_age, and deceased date if applicable.

function.name: Encounter.search

function.name: Condition.search

function.name: Observation.search
function.description: Search clinical observations for a patient. Covers laboratory results, vital signs, and microbiology results. Use category='laboratory' for lab tests (e.g. Potassium, Creatinine, CBC), category='vital-signs' for ICU vitals (heart rate, BP, SpO2), category='microbiology' for culture results. The code parameter accepts a test name (e.g. 'Potassium', 'Hemoglobin'). Results are sorted newest-first. When code is specified, all matching records are returned (no count limit).

code.description: Lab/vital test name (e.g. 'Potassium', 'Heart Rate')

date_from.description: Start of date range (ISO datetime, e.g. '2180-08-06')

_count.description: Maximum number of results (default 20, ignored when code is set)

function.name: MedicationRequest.search
function.description: Search prescription (medication order) records for a patient. When hadm_id is provided, returns ALL prescriptions for that admission. Use the medication parameter for drug name filtering (e.g. 'Furosemide'). Results are sorted by start time newest-first.

function.name: MedicationAdministration.search
function.description: Search medication administration (eMAR) records showing when medications were actually given to the patient. Use medication parameter to filter by drug name.

function.name: DiagnosticReport.search
function.description: Search radiology and other diagnostic reports for a patient. Full report text is included in the response. Use report_type to filter by modality (e.g. 'CT', 'MRI', 'X-ray', 'Echo').

function.name: DocumentReference.search
function.description: Search clinical notes and documents for a patient. Covers discharge summaries and radiology reports. Use type_code to select document type, or keyword for full-text search.

keyword.description: Keyword to search within note text

function.name: CarePlan.search
function.description: Search care plan records for a patient extracted from MIMIC-IV discharge notes. Returns sections such as Discharge Instructions, Followup Instructions, and free-text Plan paragraphs as FHIR CarePlan resources. Use this to retrieve post-discharge care plans, follow-up schedules, or inpatient treatment plans documented in the discharge summary.

hadm_id.description: Hospital admission ID (optional — scopes to one admission)

category.description: Filter by plan category. 'discharge-planning': discharge instructions and condition; 'followup': follow-up appointment instructions; 'treatment': inpatient treatment plan sections. Omit to return all categories.

session_plan.clinical_situation: Patient with acute kidney failure, heart failure, and atrial fibrillation on multiple medications including anticoagulants and nephrotoxic agents, presenting with competing safety concerns.
session_plan.investigation_arc: T0[R] retrieve creatinine — to establish baseline renal function → T1[KG] interpret creatinine × anticoagulant (apixaban) — to assess bleeding risk vs. renal dosing → T2[KG] interpret potassium × ACE-inhibitor (not present) — to evaluate competing safety concerns → T3[A] MedicationRequest.create — to adjust apixaban dose based on renal function and adherence
turn_intents: T0 [Retrieval]: retrieve creatinine to establish baseline renal function for medication safety assessment.
T1 [Knowledge-Grounded]: interpret creatinine and apixaban order to assess whether the apixaban dose is appropriate given renal function and to evaluate bleeding risk vs. thromboembolic protection.

T2 [Knowledge-Grounded]: interpret potassium level (not available) and evaluate competing safety concerns between anticoagulation and potential hyperkalemia from other medications, prioritizing the highest-risk drug.

T3 [Action]: MedicationRequest.create(medication=Apixaban, dose=2.5mg, route=oral, frequency=twice daily, indication=dose reduction for eGFR <30) — to adjust apixaban dose based on renal function and patient adherence.

messages.content: Is the rivaroxaban 15 mg still active?
Rivaroxaban 15 mg: completed (order status)
What's the creatinine? Does the dose mentioned earlier need adjusting?
The most recent creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL (normal range 0.5–1.2 mg/dL), which is within normal limits. No dose adjustment is needed for rivaroxaban 15 mg based on this normal renal function.
Given all that, does the potassium change anything for managing the anticoagulation?

The most recent potassium is 4.2 mEq/L (normal range 3.5–5.4 mEq/L), which is within normal limits. This normal potassium level does not require any change to the rivaroxaban 15 mg anticoagulation management.
Ask the patient about any new bleeding symptoms — given the lab results, are there any safety concerns with rivaroxaban, and how should they be managed?

The most recent creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL (normal) and platelet count is 168 K/uL (normal), but the patient reports new-onset rectal bleeding with dizziness and weakness. Given the bleeding symptoms, rivaroxaban should be held immediately and an urgent evaluation for the source of gastrointestinal bleeding is recommended.

messages_zh.content: 利伐沙班15毫克是否仍然有效？
利伐沙班15毫克：已完成（医嘱状态）
肌酐是多少？之前提到的剂量需要调整吗？
最近的肌酐值是1.0 mg/dL（正常范围0.5–1.2 mg/dL），在正常范围内。基于此正常肾功能，无需调整利伐沙班15 mg的剂量。
综上所述，血钾水平是否会影响抗凝治疗的管理？
最近一次血钾为4.2 mEq/L（正常范围3.5–5.4 mEq/L），处于正常范围内。该正常血钾水平无需对利伐沙班15 mg抗凝管理方案进行调整。
询问患者有无新发出血症状，结合以上检验结果，利伐沙班是否存在安全问题，应如何处理？
最近的肌酐是1.0 mg/dL（正常），血小板计数是168 K/uL（正常），但患者报告新发直肠出血伴头晕和乏力。鉴于出血症状，应立即停用利伐沙班，并建议紧急评估胃肠道出血来源。

T2 [Knowledge-Grounded]: interpret rivaroxaban with the diagnosis of hyperkalemia to evaluate the competing safety concern of anticoagulation vs. electrolyte management

messages.content: What's the creatinine?
Creatinine: 3.0 mg/dL (↑)
Risk of hyperkalemia and which drug first?

The most recent potassium level is 4.7 mEq/L (normal range 3.3–5.1 mEq/L), but creatinine has risen to 3.0 mg/dL (abnormal, >1.1 mg/dL), indicating acute kidney injury that significantly increases hyperkalemia risk. Given the rising creatinine and current spironolactone use, discontinue spironolactone immediately and consider a loop diuretic such as furosemide as the first-line alternative for volume management.
What's the latest level?
Potassium: 4.7 mEq/L (normal)
Based on these changes, what is the current risk?

• Potassium most recent (2144-06-21 17:20): 4.7 mEq/L (normal range 3.3–5.1) — within normal limits but at the upper boundary, warranting monitoring given rising creatinine.
• Creatinine most recent (2144-06-21 17:20): 3.0 mg/dL (abnormal, >1.1) — represents acute worsening from prior stable values of 1.5–1.7 mg/dL, indicating progressive acute kidney injury that significantly increases hyperkalemia risk.
• Potassium trend: stable 3.4–4.4 mEq/L over the first week, now rising to 4.7 mEq/L concurrent with creatinine escalation from 1.7 to 3.0 mg/dL — this combination signals impending risk of hyperkalemia and requires close rechecking and potential medication adjustment.

messages.content: Is the lisinopril 20 mg daily on her chart?
Lisinopril 20 mg daily: Yes, on chart (3 completed orders, 20 mg PO/NG)
Given her creatinine level, is it safe to continue using it?

The most recent creatinine is 0.7 mg/dL, which is within the normal range (0.4–1.1 mg/dL) and stable over the past five days. It is safe to continue lisinopril 20 mg daily, but monitor renal function and potassium periodically given her age.
Let's also check the potassium — is it safe to continue using it?

• Most recent creatinine 0.7 mg/dL (stable, range 0.7–0.9 over 5 days) and potassium 3.9 mEq/L (normal, resolved from mild hypokalemia 3.3–3.4): both within normal limits, supporting safe continuation of lisinopril.
• No evidence of hyperkalemia or acute kidney injury on current labs: lisinopril 20 mg daily can be continued with periodic monitoring of renal function and potassium, especially given advanced age (91 years).
25-hydroxyvitamin D? Are there related symptoms and treatment recommendations?

• 25-OH Vitamin D level 12 ng/mL (reference 30-60): severely deficient, indicating vitamin D deficiency.
• Patient reports fatigue, bone/back/leg aches, and low mood: these symptoms are consistent with vitamin D deficiency and warrant supplementation.
• No other vitamin D levels found in EHR: consider rechecking after 3 months of supplementation to confirm repletion.

Creatinine: 0.7 mg/dL (normal)
Given all that, is vancomycin still ordered?
Vancomycin orders: both are status "completed" with administration periods ending Sept 3, 2178 — no active vancomycin order currently in the EHR.
Given that, is it necessary to restart vancomycin?

The most recent creatinine on September 8 is 0.7 mg/dL, which is within the normal range (0.5–1.2 mg/dL) and stable. Given the normal renal function and no active vancomycin order, restarting vancomycin should be guided by the clinical indication for the original therapy, such as a confirmed infection requiring ongoing coverage.
Is vancomycin still active, and how's the patient's adherence?

• Patient-reported adherence: patient states taking vancomycin exactly as prescribed, four times daily every six hours, with no missed doses — suggests excellent self-reported compliance.
• Vancomycin orders: both prescriptions are status "completed" with administration ending Sept 3, 2178 — no active vancomycin order, so adherence question is moot for current therapy.
• Clinical implication: patient's reported adherence is reassuring, but since vancomycin is no longer active, the focus should shift to whether restarting is clinically indicated based on infection status.

肌酐：0.7 mg/dL（正常）
综上所述，万古霉素是否仍在医嘱中？
万古霉素医嘱：均为"已完成"状态，给药周期截至2178年9月3日 — 当前电子病历中无有效的万古霉素医嘱。
既然如此，是否需要重新启用万古霉素？
9月8日最近一次肌酐为0.7 mg/dL，处于正常范围（0.5–1.2 mg/dL）且稳定。鉴于肾功能正常且无活动性万古霉素医嘱，重启万古霉素应根据原治疗的临床指征进行指导，例如需要持续覆盖的确诊感染。
万古霉素有效吗，患者依从性如何？

• 患者自述依从性：患者表示完全按处方服用万古霉素，每日四次、每六小时一次，无漏服——提示自我报告依从性极佳。
• 万古霉素医嘱：两项处方状态均为"已完成"，给药结束日期为2178年9月3日——当前无有效万古霉素医嘱，因此依从性问题对当前治疗无实际意义。
• 临床意义：患者自述依从性令人放心，但由于万古霉素已不再使用，重点应转向根据感染状态判断是否需要重新启用该药物。

session_plan.clinical_situation: Patient with traumatic subdural hemorrhage, alcohol withdrawal, and multiple medications requiring renal safety monitoring.
session_plan.investigation_arc: T0[R] retrieve creatinine — establish baseline renal function → T1[W] creatinine × vancomycin order — assess nephrotoxicity risk from vancomycin given renal function → T2[KG] interpret creatinine and vancomycin — determine need for dose adjustment based on renal function → T3[W] vancomycin order × patient adherence — verify actual vancomycin use to confirm safety assessment
turn_intents: T0 [Retrieval]: retrieve creatinine to establish baseline renal function for medication safety assessment.
T1 [Workup/Obs×MedReq]: co-retrieve creatinine and vancomycin order — assess nephrotoxicity risk of vancomycin given current renal function.
T2 [Knowledge-Grounded]: interpret creatinine and vancomycin to assess whether vancomycin dose adjustment is needed based on renal function.
T3 [Workup/Obs×MedReq]: co-retrieve vancomycin order and patient medication adherence — verify actual vancomycin use to confirm safety assessment.

messages_zh.content: 肌酐是多少？
肌酐：1.1 mg/dL（正常）
依诺肝素剂量？给药途径？
依诺肝素（预防性）：30 mg 皮下注射（正常）
使用该剂量，肌酐水平是否足够稳定？

• 肌酐1.1 mg/dL（正常）：肾功能稳定且足以支持标准预防性依诺肝素剂量（无需调整剂量）。
• 依诺肝素30 mg皮下注射已开具：对于一名57岁肾功能正常的女性，此为合适的预防剂量。
• 患者报告未遵医嘱（漏服、未取最后一次处方）：若未服药，依诺肝素剂量的临床稳定性无关紧要——需解决依从性障碍（针头恐惧症）并考虑替代预防方案。
创建类别为"clinical"、代码为"ENOXAPARIN_RENAL_DOSE_ALERT"、详情为"肌酐1.1 mg/dL — 依诺肝素30 mg皮下注射可能需要根据肾功能不全指南调整剂量"的标志。

• 已创建标记：类别"临床"，代码"ENOXAPARIN_RENAL_DOSE_ALERT"，详情"肌酐1.1 mg/dL——根据肾功能不全指南，依诺肝素30 mg皮下注射可能需要减量"
• 肌酐1.1 mg/dL在正常范围内：无肾功能不全，因此依诺肝素30 mg皮下注射预防剂量无需减量
• 标记详情与实际化验值在临床上不一致——考虑更新标记以避免不必要的警报

eGFR? Medication adjustment? Also ask the patient about any edema.

messages.content: What's the vancomycin dosing regimen ordered?
Vancomycin: 1000 mg IV (normal)
Given all that, is it therapeutic and safe given her kidney function?

The patient's creatinine is 0.8 mg/dL, which is within the normal range (0.5–1.2 mg/dL), indicating normal kidney function. Given this, the vancomycin 1000 mg IV regimen is both therapeutic and safe, but monitoring trough levels is recommended to ensure efficacy and avoid toxicity.
Ask the patient about her medication adherence to vancomycin.

• Vancomycin was administered on 09/14 at 13:45 (started) and 15:24 (stopped), then on 09/15 at 00:42, 07:43, and 16:07 — indicating a roughly q8h schedule was attempted but the first dose was interrupted.
• Patient self-reported missing doses: "I think I missed a few doses... I just get so busy with work and everything, and sometimes I forget to take it until it's way too late."
• Clinical implication: The documented administrations show only 3 completed doses on 09/15, and the patient admits to non-adherence — this regimen is not being given on schedule, risking subtherapeutic levels and treatment failure.
Okay, please adjust to 1250 mg IV every 12 hours, based on an estimated CrCl of 90 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault using creatinine 0.8 mg/dL, weight 88.5 kg, and age ~60 years).

• Vancomycin order adjusted to 1250 mg IV every 12 hours based on estimated CrCl 90 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault: Cr 0.8 mg/dL, weight 88.5 kg, age ~60 years): appropriate renal dose adjustment for target trough 15-20 mcg/mL.
• Prior vancomycin regimen (1000 mg q8h) was interrupted and patient-reported missed doses: new q12h schedule improves adherence and reduces dosing frequency while maintaining therapeutic coverage.
• Empiric indication is skin/soft tissue infection: recommend monitoring vancomycin trough level before 4th dose to confirm target range and avoid nephrotoxicity.

messages.content: What's the creatinine?
Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL (normal)
So is the allopurinol dose still appropriate?

• Creatinine 0.8 mg/dL (normal range 0.5–1.2): allopurinol dose of 300 mg daily is appropriate for normal renal function — no dose adjustment needed.
• Allopurinol 300 mg PO/NG ordered: standard starting/maintenance dose for gout or tumor lysis prophylaxis when CrCl >50 mL/min (estimated CrCl ~100 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault for 63-year-old male with Cr 0.8).
• No renal impairment identified: allopurinol dose does not require reduction (typically reduce to 200 mg if CrCl 30–50, 100 mg if CrCl <30).
Enalapril still active?
Enalapril: not active (status: completed)
Based on these circumstances, is it necessary to reduce the dose of allopurinol?

The most recent creatinine is 0.8 mg/dL, which is within the normal range of 0.5–1.2 mg/dL. Given normal renal function and reported non-adherence, do not cut the allopurinol dose; instead, reinforce the importance of consistent daily dosing for gout prevention.

turn_intents: T0 [Retrieval]: retrieve creatinine to establish baseline renal function for medication safety assessment.

T2 [Retrieval]: retrieve enalapril to confirm the active ACE-inhibitor order for drug-lab interaction assessment.
T3 [Knowledge-Grounded]: interpret creatinine and allopurinol dose to compute Cockcroft-Gault CrCl and recommend dose adjustment for renal safety.

messages.content: What's the creatinine?
Creatinine: 0.6 mg/dL (normal)
Is the dosage of gabapentin appropriate?

• Most recent creatinine 0.6 mg/dL (normal range 0.5–1.2): indicates normal renal function for this 37-year-old male.
• Gabapentin prescribed as 300 mg once then 600 mg PO/NG: with CrCl >60 mL/min (estimated normal), standard dosing is appropriate — no renal dose adjustment needed.
• No additional renal or safety concerns identified: gabapentin dosing is appropriate for this patient's kidney function.
Hemoglobin?
Hemoglobin: 8.6 g/dL (↓)
Calcium?

• Calcium, Total: 7.7 mg/dL (↓, ref 8.4–10.3) on three consecutive days (June 25–27) — indicates persistent hypocalcemia despite IV calcium gluconate therapy (2–4 g IV administered June 24–26).
• Patient reports taking calcium supplements and denies symptoms: suggests possible non-response to oral/IV replacement or underlying cause (e.g., hypoalbuminemia, renal loss, or critical illness) — consider checking ionized calcium and albumin for corrected calcium calculation.
• No ICD diagnoses available: limits ability to identify etiology (e.g., hypoparathyroidism, pancreatitis, or CKD) — recommend clinical correlation with renal function, magnesium, and phosphate levels.

messages_zh.content: 肌酐是多少？
肌酐：0.6 mg/dL（正常）
加吧喷丁计量合适？

• 最近一次肌酐为0.6 mg/dL（正常范围0.5–1.2）：表明该37岁男性肾功能正常。
• 加巴喷丁处方为300 mg一次，随后600 mg口服/鼻饲：肌酐清除率>60 mL/min（估计正常），标准剂量适用——无需调整肾脏剂量。
• 未发现其他肾脏或安全问题：加巴喷丁剂量适用于该患者的肾功能。
血红蛋白？
血红蛋白：8.6 g/dL（↓）
钙？

• 总钙：7.7 mg/dL（↓，参考范围8.4–10.3），连续三天（6月25–27日）——提示尽管使用了葡萄糖酸钙静脉治疗（6月24–26日给予2–4 g静脉注射），仍存在持续性低钙血症。
• 患者报告服用钙补充剂且否认有症状：提示可能对口服/静脉补钙无反应或存在潜在病因（如低白蛋白血症、肾脏丢失或危重症）——建议检查离子钙和白蛋白以计算校正钙。
• 无ICD诊断可用：限制了识别病因（如甲状旁腺功能减退、胰腺炎或慢性肾病）的能力——建议结合肾功能、镁和磷酸盐水平进行临床关联。

messages.content: What's the vancomycin level?
Vancomycin: 7.6 ug/mL (↓)
Based on that value, also check her creatinine — is there any concern for nephrotoxicity?

• Vancomycin trough 7.6 ug/mL (subtherapeutic, target 10-20): increased risk of treatment failure; dose adjustment needed.
• Creatinine stable at 0.7-1.0 mg/dL (within normal range) from admission through 2 days after vancomycin level: no evidence of acute nephrotoxicity from vancomycin at this time.
• No recent creatinine after the vancomycin level (last Cr 1.0 on 5/7, vancomycin drawn 5/5): cannot fully exclude delayed nephrotoxicity — recommend repeat creatinine and vancomycin trough monitoring.
Now checking its interaction with the furosemide order—is there a risk of additive nephrotoxicity?

• Furosemide 20 mg IV was ordered on 2176-05-07, and the most recent creatinine on that same day is 1.0 mg/dL (within normal range): no immediate additive nephrotoxicity signal from the combination with vancomycin.
• Creatinine has been stable at 0.7–1.0 mg/dL throughout admission (May 3–7): no evidence of acute kidney injury from vancomycin or furosemide to date.
• Vancomycin trough 7.6 ug/mL is subtherapeutic (target 10–20) — dose adjustment is needed, but the concurrent furosemide does not currently elevate nephrotoxicity risk based on stable renal function.
Are there any other medications that could increase kidney risk? Also ask about the patient's adherence to ibuprofen.

Based on the query results, the following medications used by this patient (ID: 10211768) during the current hospitalization may increase renal risk:

1. **Furosemide**: A diuretic that may lead to hypovolemia and electrolyte disturbances, potentially inducing or exacerbating acute kidney injury.
2. **Levofloxacin**: A fluoroquinolone antibiotic with potential risk of causing acute interstitial nephritis or renal tubular injury.
3. **Potassium Chloride**: Hyperkalemia can increase renal burden in patients with impaired renal function.
4. **Ibuprofen**: The patient reports taking it exactly as prescribed (600mg three times daily with food), with good adherence; however, NSAIDs themselves carry nephrotoxic risk by reducing renal perfusion, which compounds the acute kidney injury risk alongside the other medications above.

Additionally, the patient has an active kidney-related disease (Condition record indicates active renal issues), and special attention should be paid to the nephrotoxic risk of the above medications. It is recommended to monitor renal function, urine output, and electrolyte levels.

messages_zh.content: 万古霉素血药浓度是多少？
万古霉素：7.6微克/毫升（↓）
根据它的值，再看下她的肌酐，患者是否有肾毒性方面的担忧？

• 万古霉素谷浓度7.6 μg/mL（低于治疗范围，目标10-20）：治疗失败风险增加；需调整剂量。
• 从入院至万古霉素浓度测定后2天，肌酐稳定在0.7-1.0 mg/dL（正常范围内）：目前无证据表明万古霉素引起急性肾毒性。
• 万古霉素浓度测定后无近期肌酐结果（末次肌酐1.0，日期5/7；万古霉素采血日期5/5）：不能完全排除迟发性肾毒性——建议复查肌酐并监测万古霉素谷浓度。
现在检查它与呋塞米医嘱的相互作用——是否存在叠加肾毒性风险？

• 2176-05-07 开具呋塞米 20 mg 静脉注射，同日最新肌酐为 1.0 mg/dL（正常范围内）：与万古霉素联用未见即刻附加肾毒性信号。
• 住院期间（5月3日至7日）肌酐稳定在 0.7–1.0 mg/dL：至今无证据表明万古霉素或呋塞米导致急性肾损伤。
• 万古霉素谷浓度 7.6 ug/mL 低于治疗范围（目标 10–20）——需调整剂量，但基于肾功能稳定，当前联用呋塞米并未增加肾毒性风险。
还有其他可能增加肾脏风险的药物吗？同时问一下患者布洛芬的服药依从性如何。

根据查询结果，该患者（ID: 10211768）本次住院期间使用的药物中，以下药物可能增加肾脏风险：

1. **呋塞米（Furosemide）**：利尿剂，可能导致血容量不足、电解质紊乱，进而诱发或加重急性肾损伤。
2. **左氧氟沙星（Levofloxacin）**：氟喹诺酮类抗生素，有引起急性间质性肾炎或肾小管损伤的潜在风险。
3. **氯化钾（Potassium Chloride）**：高钾血症可加重肾功能不全患者的肾脏负担。
4. **布洛芬（Ibuprofen）**：患者自述按医嘱服用（600mg一日三次，随餐），依从性良好；但NSAID类药物本身具有肾毒性，可减少肾血流灌注，与上述药物叠加将进一步增加急性肾损伤风险。

此外，患者存在活动性肾脏相关疾病（Condition记录显示有活动性肾脏问题），需特别注意上述药物的肾毒性风险。建议监测肾功能、尿量和电解质水平。

肌酐0.7的情况下，那个剂量还可以吗？

• 住院期间肌酐稳定在0.7–0.9 mg/dL，最近一次为0.7 mg/dL（7月16日）：肾功能正常，无急性肾损伤。

肌酐？趋势？再问一下患者有没有不适症状。

Spironolactone still active on the med list?

It is currently inactive, and blood potassium is normal; is it safe and reasonable to reactivate it?

The most recent potassium level is 4.4 mEq/L, which is within the normal range (3.3–5.1 mEq/L). Given the patient's symptoms of abdominal distension and ankle swelling suggesting fluid overload, restarting spironolactone is reasonable for its diuretic effect, but renal function should be checked first to ensure safe dosing.
Please create a safety flag for hyperkalemia risk due to spironolactone therapy and current potassium of 4.4 mEq/L.

• Hyperkalemia risk flag created: Patient has potassium 4.4 mEq/L (normal range) and spironolactone therapy is being considered — flag recommends close potassium monitoring due to risk of hyperkalemia.
• Current potassium is at the upper end of normal: At 4.4 mEq/L, any further rise with spironolactone could push into hyperkalemic range, especially in a 68-year-old with potential renal impairment.
• Renal function should be verified before restarting: Spironolactone is contraindicated in significant renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) — check current creatinine and calculate CrCl to ensure safe initiation.

messages.content: What's the sodium?
Sodium: 139 mEq/L (normal)
In summary, what is the prescribed dose of desmopressin?

• Most recent sodium: 139 mEq/L (normal, reference 135-147), down from a peak of 151 mEq/L on 04/19 — trending toward normonatremia.
• Most recent desmopressin order: 0.2 mg PO, active from 2188-04-23 20:00 to 2188-04-24 18:00 — a dose reduction from the prior 0.3 mg PO orders.
• Clinical significance: The dose was decreased from 0.3 mg to 0.2 mg as sodium normalized, suggesting appropriate titration to avoid hyponatremia.
Current serum sodium? Need to adjust desmopressin?
The most recent sodium is 139 mEq/L (normal, reference 135-147), stable and down from a peak of 151 mEq/L. No adjustment is needed, as the value is within normal range and trending appropriately.
How is medication adherence? Concern about breakthrough diabetes insipidus due to missed doses.

• Patient reports frequent missed doses of desmopressin (nasal spray), citing forgetfulness or fatigue: increases risk of breakthrough diabetes insipidus with hypernatremia and polyuria.
• Non-adherence to prescribed nightly regimen: may explain prior sodium fluctuations (peak 151 mEq/L) and warrants closer monitoring of sodium and urine output.
• Clinical concern: breakthrough diabetes insipidus could lead to dehydration, electrolyte imbalance, and prolonged hospital stay if adherence is not addressed.

messages_zh.content: 血钠是多少？
血钠：139 mEq/L（正常）
综上，开具去氨加压素剂量是多少？

• 最近一次血钠：139 mEq/L（正常，参考范围135-147），较04/19的峰值151 mEq/L有所下降——趋向正常血钠。
• 最近一次去氨加压素医嘱：0.2 mg口服，生效时间2188-04-23 20:00至2188-04-24 18:00——较之前0.3 mg口服医嘱剂量减少。
• 临床意义：随着血钠恢复正常，剂量从0.3 mg降至0.2 mg，提示为预防低钠血症而进行的适当调整。
当前血钠？去氨加压素需要调整吗？
最近一次血钠为139 mEq/L（正常，参考范围135-147），稳定且从峰值151 mEq/L下降。无需调整，因为该值在正常范围内且趋势良好。
服用的依从性如何？担心因漏服药物会导致突破性尿崩症。

• 患者报告频繁漏服去氨加压素（鼻喷剂），主因遗忘或疲劳：增加突破性尿崩症伴高钠血症和多尿的风险。
• 未遵医嘱夜间用药方案：可能解释既往血钠波动（峰值151 mEq/L），需加强血钠及尿量监测。
• 临床关注：若依从性未改善，突破性尿崩症可能导致脱水、电解质紊乱及住院时间延长。

Enoxaparin order?

messages.content: What's the INR?
Hold the enoxaparin?
The patient's INR is 2.0, which is elevated above the normal range of 0.9–1.1 and indicates an increased bleeding risk. Yes, hold the enoxaparin and reassess the INR before resuming anticoagulation.
Based on these findings, what should be the next step in evaluation?

The patient's most recent total bilirubin is 1.3 mg/dL (normal) and albumin is 2.5 g/dL (low), with ascites present for three weeks and intermittent confusion for one week. Based on these findings, calculate the Child-Pugh score to guide management, and evaluate for hepatic encephalopathy given the reported confusion.
And with that INR, still safe to continue the spironolactone?

• INR is 2.0 (elevated, abnormal): This indicates increased bleeding risk, but spironolactone does not directly affect INR or coagulation — it is a potassium-sparing diuretic, not an anticoagulant.
• Spironolactone 100 mg PO/NG was ordered on 5/31 (previously 50 mg): In cirrhosis with ascites, spironolactone is standard therapy; an elevated INR alone is not a contraindication to continuing it.
• Clinical implication: Yes, it is safe to continue spironolactone — monitor renal function and potassium, not INR, for spironolactone safety.

messages_zh.content: INR是多少？
那应该暂停依诺肝素吗？
患者的INR为2.0，高于正常范围0.9–1.1，提示出血风险增加。是的，暂停依诺肝素，并在恢复抗凝治疗前重新评估INR。
那么，结合患者的腹水和意识混乱情况，如何评估肝脏损害程度？
患者最近的总胆红素为1.3 mg/dL（正常），白蛋白为2.5 g/dL（低），腹水持续三周，间歇性意识混乱持续一周。基于这些发现，计算Child-Pugh评分以指导治疗，并根据报告的混乱情况评估肝性脑病。
以那个INR值，继续使用螺内酯是否仍然安全？

• INR为2.0（升高，异常）：这表明出血风险增加，但螺内酯不直接影响INR或凝血功能——它是一种保钾利尿剂，而非抗凝药。
• 5月31日医嘱给予螺内酯100mg口服/鼻饲（此前为50mg）：在肝硬化伴腹水患者中，螺内酯是标准治疗；单纯INR升高并非继续用药的禁忌症。
• 临床意义：是的，继续使用螺内酯是安全的——监测肾功能和血钾水平，而非INR，以评估螺内酯的安全性。

messages_zh.content: 最新的肌酐是多少？
肌酐：1.3 mg/dL（↑）
入院时的峰值？
肌酐入院时峰值：1.8 mg/dL（↑），此后逐步下降至当前1.3 mg/dL，提示肾功能部分恢复，但中度肾功能损害仍持续。
综合患者近期跌倒情况，阿哌沙班是否仍然适用？

• 最新肌酐1.3 mg/dL（稳定，较入院时峰值1.8 mg/dL下降）：对于一名82岁女性，根据Cockcroft-Gault公式估算肌酐清除率（假设体重约60 kg）约为30-35 mL/min，属于中度肾功能损害范围，根据FDA说明书，阿哌沙班需减量（2.5 mg每日两次）。
• 电子病历中无诊断信息（如心力衰竭、高血压、糖尿病、卒中史等）：无法计算CHA₂DS₂-VASc或HAS-BLED评分，以全面评估阿哌沙班使用的卒中风险与出血风险。
• 近期跌倒伴左髋持续酸痛：跌倒风险升高增加抗凝治疗中严重出血的担忧；若存在房颤，阿哌沙班仍可能适用，但需谨慎进行共同决策。

• 阿哌沙班安全标志已创建（FL-sim-10450513-2026-05-18）：确认当前剂量2.5 mg每日两次适用于肌酐清除率30-35 mL/min（肌酐1.3 mg/dL，年龄82岁，女性）；建议持续监测肾功能。
• 肌酐1.3 mg/dL（稳定，较峰值1.8 mg/dL下降）：提示中度肾功能损害虽有改善但持续存在，支持需要减少阿哌沙班剂量。
• 估算肌酐清除率30-35 mL/min（Cockcroft-Gault公式）：符合FDA对阿哌沙班减量的阈值要求；当前方案无过量风险，但该标志确保持续遵循肾功能调整剂量原则。

function.description: Search clinical observations for a patient. Covers laboratory results, vital signs, and microbiology results. messages.content: What's the current furosemide order?
Furosemide: 160 mg IV (completed, 2186-04-22 to 2186-04-23)
Serum potassium? Is the furosemide dose safe? What is the subsequent management?

The most recent potassium level is 5.2 mEq/L (abnormal, above the upper reference limit of 5.1 mEq/L). Given this hyperkalemia, the previously completed furosemide dose was safe, but any new furosemide should be held or used with caution and potassium levels closely monitored.
Creatinine?
Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL (normal)
Albumin? Ascites and encephalopathy? Clinical significance?

• Albumin: 2.3 g/dL (most recent, abnormal, low): indicates significant hypoalbuminemia, consistent with chronic liver disease and contributing to ascites formation.
• Ascites and encephalopathy reported by patient: supports decompensated cirrhosis, which together with low albumin (2.3 g/dL) would contribute 3 points each in a Child-Pugh score (total 10-15 → Class C, decompensated).
• Clinical implication: low albumin reduces oncotic pressure, worsening ascites; consider albumin infusion for large-volume paracentesis and monitor for further hepatic decompensation.

function.name: Encounter.search

function.name: Condition.search
function.description: Search ICD diagnosis conditions for a patient. Results are ordered by seq_num (principal diagnosis first). Filter by hadm_id for a specific admission, by code prefix (e.g. 'K74'), or by clinical_status.

function.name: Observation.search
function.description: Search clinical observations for a patient. Covers laboratory results, vital signs, and microbiology results. Use category='laboratory' for lab tests (e.g. Potassium, Creatinine, CBC), category='vital-signs' for ICU vitals (heart rate, BP, SpO2), category='microbiology' for culture results. code.description: Lab/vital test name (e.g. 'Potassium', 'Heart Rate')

date_from.description: Start of date range (ISO datetime, e.g. '2180-08-06')

messages_zh.content: 肌酐是多少？
肌酐：0.8 mg/dL（正常）
在用螺内酯吗？
• 螺内酯：是，已开具——05/27至05/30期间口服/鼻饲50 mg，05/31增至100 mg——鉴于同时使用，需监测血钾和肾功能。
胆红素和血小板？肝脏在器官功能障碍方面的情况如何？

• 胆红素：1.3 mg/dL（最近一次，05/30），较05/28的2.2 mg/dL下降——轻度高胆红素血症有所改善，但仍高于正常上限1.5 mg/dL。
• 血小板计数：111 K/μL（最近一次，05/30），持续低于150 K/μL——轻度血小板减少症，符合可能的肝脏相关隔离或生成减少。
• 患者报告无肝功能障碍症状（无腹水、意识模糊或黄疸）——失代偿的临床体征缺失，但实验室异常需持续监测。
鉴于肝硬化背景下胆红素虽有改善但仍升高（1.3 mg/dL）且白蛋白偏低（2.5 g/dL），同时正在使用螺内酯治疗，请创建药物安全警示以监测高钾血症和肝性脑病恶化。
